title: What We Learned from Using LLMs in Pinterest — Mukuntha Narayanan, Han Wang, Pinterest

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary focus is search relevance modeling, reranking architecture, embedding-based retrieval, and ranking at Pinterest, which is the core of retrieval and search systems. Pinterest is a visual discovery and search platform handling billions of queries across corpora in 45+ languages, fitting the search and knowledge domain. The talk covers model fine-tuning and distillation in development, ablation studies and online results in evaluation, production serving with caching in deployment, and 100x data scaling across markets. Prerequisites include familiarity with recommendation system architecture, encoder model architectures, and knowledge distillation, indicating intermediate-level content. This is a conference presentation delivered at the AI Engineer channel about production lessons from deploying LLMs in Pinterest search. summary: Pinterest search handles over 6 billion monthly searches across billions of pins in 45+ languages and 100+ countries. The search backend follows a standard architecture with query understanding, retrieval, ranking, and blending stages, with the relevance model sitting at the reranking stage right before blending to produce the final feed. The relevance model is a classifier predicting pin-query relevance on a 5-point scale using a cross-encoder structure. The presenters share four main learnings. First, LLMs are effective at relevance prediction: fine-tuning open-source LLMs on internal data yields substantial improvements, with an 8B Llama model achieving 12% improvement over multilingual BERT and 20% over Pinterest's SearchSage embedding model. Second, building robust text representations requires combining pin titles/descriptions, VLM-generated image captions, board titles from user-curated boards, and high-engagement search queries. Ablation studies confirm each feature contributes incremental gains, with user-action features proving especially valuable. Third, knowledge distillation enables production deployment without prohibitive costs. A teacher LLM cross-encoder is fine-tuned on limited human-labeled data, then used to label samples from daily search logs, scaling training data 100x across domains, languages, and countries via semi-supervised learning. The student bi-encoder computes pin embeddings offline and query embeddings in real-time with approximately 85% cache hit rate, keeping query latency to a few milliseconds. Fourth, relevance-tuned LLM embeddings serve as general-purpose semantic representations reused across Pinterest surfaces including related pins and home feed. Q&A reveals that LLM adoption was driven by VLM captions enabling expansion beyond limited markets for relevance data and multilingual models generating synthetic data for different markets. The embedding model is not inherently multimodal but visual captions effectively capture image content. A single multilingual model serves all languages, leveraging cross-language transfer.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: LLMs substantially improve search relevance prediction over traditional embedding models, with 8B Llama achieving 12% gain over multilingual BERT and 20% over SearchSage
VLM-generated image captions provide a strong baseline for pin text representation and enable expansion beyond limited markets for collecting relevance data
User action features such as board titles and high-engagement queries serve as valuable content annotations that incrementally improve relevance prediction
Knowledge distillation from a cross-encoder teacher to a bi-encoder student enables cost-effective production serving at Pinterest scale
Semi-supervised learning using daily search logs scales training data 100x across domains, languages, and countries beyond limited human-labeled data
A single multilingual LLM serves all languages, leveraging cross-language transfer rather than maintaining separate per-language models
The embedding model is not inherently multimodal; visual captions effectively capture image content, though true multimodality is being explored
Relevance-tuned LLM embeddings transfer well to other Pinterest surfaces including related pins and home feed as general-purpose semantic representations

How to build robust pin text representations combining VLM captions, user actions, and metadata

sections.title: Introduction to Pinterest and search statistics
sections.summary: Pinterest is a visual discovery platform with home feed, related pins, and search surfaces. Search handles over 6 billion monthly searches across billions of pins in 45+ languages and 100+ countries, motivating investment in search relevance.

sections.title: Search backend architecture overview
sections.summary: Pinterest search backend follows a standard recommendation system architecture with query understanding, retrieval, ranking, and blending stages. The talk focuses on semantic relevance modeling at the reranking stage.

sections.title: Search relevance model architecture
sections.summary: The relevance model is a classifier predicting pin-query relevance on a 5-point scale using a cross-encoder structure that concatenates query and pin text, passes through an LLM for embeddings, and feeds into an MLP layer.

sections.title: Lesson 1: LLMs are good at relevance prediction
sections.summary: Fine-tuning open-source LLMs on internal Pinterest data substantially improves relevance prediction. The 8B Llama model achieves 12% improvement over multilingual BERT and 20% over SearchSage, with performance scaling as model size increases.

sections.title: Lesson 2: VLM captions and user actions as content annotations
sections.summary: Pin text representation combines titles/descriptions, VLM-generated image captions, board titles, and high-engagement queries. Ablation studies show VLM captions provide a solid baseline, and user-action features add significant incremental gains as content annotations.

sections.title: Lesson 3: Knowledge distillation for production serving
sections.summary: A teacher LLM cross-encoder is fine-tuned on limited human labels, then labels daily search log samples to scale training data 100x via semi-supervised learning. The student bi-encoder computes pin embeddings offline and query embeddings online with ~85% cache hit rate, achieving international relevance and search fulfillment gains.

sections.title: Lesson 4: Relevance-tuned embeddings as general-purpose representations
sections.summary: Pin and query embeddings from the production student model serve as free general-purpose semantic representations, performing well across related pins, home feed, and other Pinterest surfaces.

sections.title: Key takeaways recap and Q&A
sections.summary: Recap of four lessons. Q&A covers open-source LLM selection via experimentation and clarifies that LLMs distill into a student model predicting search relevance served at the end of the search pipeline.

sections.title: Extended Q&A: Architecture, multimodality, and multilingual approach
sections.summary: Q&A clarifies the relevance model sits at the reranking stage right before blending. LLM adoption was driven by VLM captions enabling expansion beyond limited markets and multilingual models generating synthetic data for different markets. The embedding model is not inherently multimodal but visual captions effectively capture image content. A single multilingual model serves all languages, leveraging cross-language transfer.

demonstrations: Ablation study showing incremental relevance gains from sequentially adding text features (VLM captions, board titles, engagement queries)
Online results showing relevance and search fulfillment gains across US, Germany, and France segments

limitations: Human-labeled training data predominantly comes from the US, limiting direct supervision for international markets
Large LLM cross-encoder teacher models are too expensive for direct online serving
Cross-encoder architecture does not scale well for real-time serving due to cross-interaction requirements
The embedding model is not inherently multimodal, relying on VLM captions rather than direct image embedding
